title: Cross-origin prompts still have significant use cases
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/timers-and-user-prompts.html#simple-dialogs

> If window's relevant settings object's origin and window's relevant settings object's top\-level origin are not same origin\-domain, then return true\.

I don't think that sufficient considerations were made here, particularly here:

> Given the low usage of cross-origin iframe JS dialogs

Cross-origin prompts (including confirm()) are used in many cases to create a way to confirm an action from an iframed document (often a plugin) that isn't clickjackable. Often this is used on a different subdomain of the main domain, or in CMS/Salesforce plugins. My particular case was Hatena Star and Hatena Blog, where a confirm prompt must be completed before permitting the user action (add star/subscribe to blog) to complete.

It's not always easy to protect sensitive actions while still providing users with enhanced customizability such as a custom domain name and custom JS. In several blog platforms, an iframe is used to confirm protected user actions such as subscribing. In these cases, the ability to use confirm() in cross-origin iframes is vital.

The primary reasoning for the removal of this functionality seems to be centered around simplifying UI and protecting users from themselves, but it really just opens up security issues.

There's another thing this breaks: save-or-discard functionality in iframed rich text editors, another important function of any blogging platform. Since the default action is to return false, if a dialog is presented asking "You have unsaved changes. Do you want to save them?" and it's automatically returning false, then this will cause loss of user data due to the nullification of those protections.

I'm not seeing any provision in the updated spec for permitting it with CSP or anything similar. Maybe this is based upon the assumption that this functionality is primarily used by malicious actors. That said, it seems that this change (in latest Chrome) affects even iframes which share an apex domain but are on different subdomains.

Thank you for your consideration.
